newsitem.title: UK: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.
newsitem.headline: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the air cargo industry in the week January 24 - January 31.
**JANUARY 24**
FRANKFURT - German freight forwarder Hellmann International Forwarders has added new partners in Finland and Bulgaria to its international co-operation network.

KUALA LUMPUR - Kuala Lumpur International airport Bhd, which is building a 9.0 billion ringgit airport south of the capital signed a 2.2 billion ringgit Islamic bond issue to help finance the project.
MEXICO CITY - Decio de Mara Serrano, deputy minister for foreign trade says Mexico's trade ministry hopes the country's exports will rise by 15 percent in 1997 over 1996.

CARACAS - Anger over Venezuela's struggling national airline Viasa grew as ministers prepared for talks with the Spanish government in an attempt to save the partly Spanish-owned carrier from bankruptcy.
COPENHAGEN - SAS says that punctuality improved in 1996, but that weather and computer problems were causing problems and quality targets would not be reached until spring.
FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla - The FAA issued an emergency order revoking the operating certificate of Aero Flight Services of Fort Lauderdale
SEATTLE - Boeing denied reports suggesting that it had shelved plans to produce a bigger version of its 747 jumbo jet to concentrate on developing a futuristic superjumbo with twice the capacity.
ZURICH - Swisscargo Ltd raised its cargo rates an average of 15 Swiss centimes per kg as of March 1.
KITZBUEHEL - Vienna airport operator Flughafen Wien expectsd net profit to fall to 602 million schillings from 673 million a year ago, but still plans to pay a higher dividend.
KIEV - A senior government official says Ukraine will decide next week whether U.S. planemaker Boeing or Airbus will win a tender to replace Air Ukraine's ageing fleet.

CHICAGO - Illinois transportation officials outlined financing options for a new airport southwest of Chicago that they said could be built for a total cost of $342 million to $2.7 billion, largely using general airport revenue bonds.
CALGARY - Canadian Airlines says it planned to boost service between major aviation hubs in Canada and the United States in the final stage of its North American route restructuring.
ATLANTA - UPS says daily express volume for its domestic and international operations was up 9.5 percent in 1996 compared with volume in 1995.
SEATTLE - Boeing says Douglas Beighle, senior vice president and chief administrative officer, has decided to retire from the company on May 1.

FRANKFURT - Demand trends for air travel, passenger strategies for airlines and airports, and intermodal linking of rail and air transport are the main themes of a passenger travel conference in Frankfurt next month.
* German freight forwarder Hellmann International Forwarders says it has added new partners in Finland and Bulgaria to its international co-operation network.

NEW DELHI - The Indian government says it approved a domestic aviation policy allowing foreign investors to take equity stakes of up to 40 percent in domestic airlines, but analysts said it fell short of expectations.
**JANUARY 25**
VALLETTA - Prime Minister Alfred Sant says Air Malta made a loss of $2.7 million on its core operations in the financial year that ended last March.
PARIS - Newspaper Le Monde says France is seeking an agreement with Beijing to allow Europe's Ariane rocket to be used as a back-up in case of failure of China's Long March launcher.
WELLINGTON - The New Zealand Press Association says Ansett New Zealand is expected to report another profit despite high fuel costs and traffic disruptions caused by had weather and congestion,

NEW DELHI - Analysts says on India's new domestic aviation policy, which keeps the door shut on foreign airlines, sends confusing signals to investors and underlines the divisions in the ruling coalition.
